This means that only applicants who are placed high enough in the ranking will be admitted — for instance, the 20 highest-scoring applicants for a programme accepting a maximum of 20 students. 1. ApplicationSubmit your application and pay the admission fee within the application deadline.2. Admission Test or InterviewTake the admission test or attend the interview. Be sure to carefully follow the instructions outlined in the programme’s Call for applications, along with any additional communications from the Academic Board.For visa applicants: please refer to the Call for applications to check whether, as a visa applicant, you are exempt from taking the admission test or attending the interview.3. Ranking & EligibilityAfter the test or interview, check the ranking on the programme’s website to see whether you have scored high enough for admission. If your name appears among those admitted, you are now eligible to proceed with enrolment.We remind you that admitted students have only a few days to enrol after the ranking is published. Please read the Call for applications carefully to make sure that you don’t miss the enrolment deadline.4. Credentials EvaluationWhile you move through the process, our offices will formally verify your foreign qualification to ensure that:it makes you eligible to enrol in a Master’s degree in Italyit was issued by a legitimate and officially recognised higher education institution.The duration of this phase may vary, depending on how clear your documents are, how many applications are being processed, and how easy it is to retrieve information on institutions and qualifications.Please don’t contact us for updates on the evaluation of your credentials. We will be the ones contacting you if we need you to submit additional documents or information.Remember: your enrolment will remain conditional until you submit all required documents and we fully verify their authenticity. Select your category EU or EU-equivalent with foreign qualification Choose this category if: you are a citizen of a European Union (EU) member state, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, or San Marino; you are a non-EU citizen with a valid Italian residence card (or residence permit application receipt); you have dual citizenship, including one from a EU country non-EU residing abroad with foreign qualification (visa app) Choose this category if you are not a citizen of a European Union (EU) member state, you reside abroad, and you will apply for an Italian student visa Marco Polo Choose this category if you have a Chinese citizenship and you are part of the Marco Polo programme Why do we ask this?
